{{nihongo|'''Iwatsutsukowake Shrine'''|石都々古和気神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

* {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|Q506610|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Mikoto}}（あじすきたかひこねのみこと）

; Associated deities
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}（おおくにぬしのみこと）
* {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Homuda-wake-no-Mikoto}}（ほんだわけのみこと、{{ill|Hachiman|ar|هاتشيمان|az|Haçiman|ca|Hachiman|de|Hachiman|el|Χατσίμαν|es|Hachiman|eu|Hachiman|fa|هاچیمان|fi|Hachiman|fr|Hachiman|hu|Hacsiman|id|Hachiman|it|Hachiman|ja|八幡神|ko|하치만 신|mni|ꯍꯆꯤꯃꯥꯟ|my|ဟချိမန်း|pl|Hachiman|pt|Hachiman|ru|Хатиман|simple|Hachiman|sl|Hačiman|sv|Hachiman|tok|jan sewi Kasiman|tr|Hachiman|uk|Хачіман|uz|Hachiman|vi|Hachiman|wuu|八幡神|zh|八幡神|qid=Q261637}}）

The original deity is Ajisukitakahikone-no-Mikoto. The same deity is enshrined at {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsutsukowake Shrine}} in {{ill|Tanagura, Fukushima|Q1155858|qid=Q1155858}}, and there is a theory this shrine was divided from there, though no clear proof exists.

== History ==
This shrine stands on the summit of a mountain called Hachiman-yama. Its founding date is unknown, but many sacred rocks remain on the mountain, indicating it had long been a ritual site. It is regarded as a candidate for "Iwatsutsukowake Shrine in Shirakawa District, Mutsu Province" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, which is its first appearance in written records.

In Eishō 6 ({{ill|1051|Q19363|qid=Q19363}}), {{ill|Minamoto no Arimitsu|Q11564122|qid=Q11564122}} joined {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}} in suppressing the Abe clan and, for merit, received Ishikawa lands as steward. In Kōhei 6 ({{ill|1063|Q19400|qid=Q19400}}), he moved here, took the name Ishikawa Aritsura, and built Mitsuashi Castle (Ishikawa Castle) east of this shrine on Hachiman-yama summit. For 25 generations over 528 years this was the seat of the {{ill|Ishikawa clan of Mutsu|Q11658603|qid=Q11658603}}, until confiscated by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. In Jiryaku 2 ({{ill|1066|Q19411|qid=Q19411}}), a divided spirit from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|Q710098|qid=Q710098}} (Hachiman deity and Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto) was enshrined together at Iwatsutsukowake Shrine.

== Rituals ==
The day Hachiman deity was enshrined together was the old calendar 9th month, 19th day, and since then the annual festival was held on that day. The {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} carrying the sacred body descended from the summit to Umaba-chō temporary hall, where rituals such as {{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157}} were held for seven days. In 1975 (Shōwa 50), festival dates were changed to September 11-15 (new calendar). In 2003 (Heisei 15), the annual ceremony was moved to the second Saturday of September, with the prior three days as participation days.

== Cultural properties ==
== Fukushima Prefecture designated cultural property ==
* Crocodile-mouth ornament of Iwatsutsukowake Shrine (fine craft) - a bronze ornament dedicated by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ishikawa Mochimitsu}} in Ōei 30 (1423), designated 1 October 1953<ref name="石川町">[http://www.town.ishikawa.fukushima.jp/admin/hall/02/01/01/04.html Medieval cultural properties of Ishikawa Town] Ishikawa Town</ref>.

== Ishikawa Town designated cultural properties ==
* One pair of Iwatsutsukowake Shrine komainu (sculpture) - a pair called "flying lion-dogs," made in 1930 (Shōwa 5) by stonemason {{ill|Kobayashi Wahei|Q11461468|qid=Q11461468}}, designated in May 2016<ref>[http://www.town.ishikawa.fukushima.jp/info/005321.html "Iwatsutsukowake Shrine komainu" newly designated as town cultural property] Ishikawa Town</ref>.
* Yoshida Kōichi documents (old documents) - historical documents owned by Yoshida Kōichi, priest of Iwatsutsukowake Shrine and first mayor of Ishikawa Town; designated 25 March 1991<ref name="石川町"/>.

== Access ==
* About 10 minutes on foot from {{ill|Iwaki-Ishikawa Station|Q11587873|qid=Q11587873}} on the {{ill|Suigun Line|de|Suigun-Linie|es|Línea Suigun|fr|Ligne Suigun|it|Linea Suigun|ja|水郡線|ko|스이군선|tl|Linyang Suigun|zh|水郡線|qid=Q1056202}} ({{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071}})

From the precinct entrance to the honden is about a 10-minute mountain path. Separate from the approach, there is a road for cars up to beside the honden.
